title: TensorCore hybrid-LRU eviction + cooperative prefetch notes
summary: Working notes exploring a hybrid LRU eviction strategy for paged KV combined with cooperative cross-warp prefetching and TensorCore-friendly fused attention kernels. Goal: keep 99th latency SLOs under memory pressure while enabling tensor-core matmul paths for quantized models.
background: We have several kernel experiments focused on paged KV + FlashAttention-style fused ops. Current problems: (1) Thrashing when multiple long-context queries interleave and cause repeated KV page faults; (2) TensorCore matmuls (FP16/INT8) are underutilized because we break compute into small kernels for prefetch/eviction coordination; (3) Eviction decisions are coarse-grained and don't account for short-lived hotspots. This doc sketches an approach that sits between fully LRU and purely recency-agnostic eviction: a hybrid LRU with hotspot detection and cooperative cross-warp prefetch to amortize paging latency.
design_notes:
1) Hybrid LRU with recency buckets:
   - Maintain per-GPU lightweight recency buckets: hot / warm / cold. On page access, promote page into hot if accessed multiple times within a short epoch. Eviction prefers cold pages across all contexts.
   - Use an approx counting bloom/tiny sketch per-page to detect hotspots (2-4 bit saturating counters) to avoid global LRU cost.

2) Ephemeral hotspot windowing:
   - Short window (e.g., 256-1024 requests or ~100ms) to consider a page 'ephemeral-hot'. Pages in ephemeral-hot get an eviction immunity timer. Purpose: avoid evicting pages that are repeatedly accessed in short bursts by e.g., a single conversation.

3) Cooperative cross-warp prefetch:
   - When kernel A (attention forward) detects an upcoming sequence length that will require a KV page not resident, it emits a prefetch intent into a lightweight shared queue in GPU L2/global mem.
   - Subsequent warps/blocks check the queue and can prefetch a page proactively if they have spare cycles. This reduces stalls for the immediate warp and spreads bandwidth load.

4) Kernel splitting for TensorCore throughput:
   - Separate the compute into two logical kernels: a small control kernel (prefetch/kv-check + issuance) and a heavy compute kernel (tensor-core fused attention). The control kernel runs with a few threads per CTA to manage paging and decisions; the compute kernel assumes pages are resident.
   - Use persistent-CTA style launch for compute kernel to keep TensorCores busy and issue worklets as pages become available.

5) Quantization-aware tiling:
   - For INT8/4 paths, tile matmuls to align warps/CTA to tensor-core shapes (e.g., 16x8 blocks) and ensure load/store coalescing even for spilled pages. Incorporate small dequantization-on-load when bringing a page in to avoid extra memory passes.
microbenchmarks:
Planned microbenchmarks:
- Single-stream long-context (seq=32..16k): measure page fault frequency, avg page residency, 95/99 latency for token generation.
- Multi-stream interleaved: 8-32 concurrent contexts with bursts; measure thrash rate and overall throughput.
- Prefetch backpressure test: synthetic kernel that issues many prefetch intents to saturate PCIe/NVLink; measure queue growth and eviction cycles.
- TensorCore utilization: instrument occupancy and tensor-core SM utilization with/without kernel split and with different tiling params.
- Quantized paths: end-to-end latency for INT8 matmul vs FP16 for identical sequence shapes.

Metrics to capture: page_faults_per_k_token, avg_page_fetch_time(ms), eviction_count/s, avg_eviction_age, tensorcore_sm_util, kernel_idle_cycles, PCIe_bandwidth_util.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Extra complexity: introducing a queue and cooperative prefetch semantics increases code complexity and potential correctness issues (ordering between fetch and compute). Need strong asserts + debug builds.
- PCIe/NVLink bandwidth pressure: prefetching can worsen congestion if not rate-limited. Must incorporate adaptive prefetch throttling based on measured bandwidth and queue depth.
- Starvation: persistent worker CTAs should yield if compute demand is high; otherwise we may steal cycles from critical attention kernels.
- Memory overhead: ephemeral immunity/tiny counters add ~5-8 bytes per page; acceptable but must be accounted for large models.
- Performance variance: heuristic parameters (window size, bucket thresholds) likely model/workload-dependent; require autotuning or per-tenant profiles.
open_questions:
1) Should eviction decisions consider model/caller priority? (i.e., preempt low-priority tenant pages) -- ties into SLO-based routing.
2) What is the right size for ephemeral window? start with 100ms heuristic but need benchmarks across workloads.
3) How to safely coordinate across multiple GPUs for multi-GPU KV sharding? Shared queue needs to be per-GPU; cross-device prefetch expensive.
4) Failure modes: if async_fetch_page fails or is very slow, how do we degrade? immediate fallback to smaller model variant?
5) Can we integrate with existing trace/span framework to signal page-level cost into Console for per-route cost attribution?

notes_to_self: Keep debug-only strong invariants: page_table checksum after each async fetch, eviction must not free a page marked in-use by a running kernel. If race observed, fallback to coarse-grain global lock in debug builds. Also add per-CTA telemetry counters to help root-cause thrash.
